fields.AN_Notes: General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'Writing clear and detailed prompts to generate relevant and personalised content for youth.' and 'Training youth workers to divide information clearly and into defined blocks - prompts - will make it easier for AI systems to understand and process their input.' (Portugal focus group, Q4 and Q5). Population: youth work is coded as part of child and youth services (Child_Family_Welfare) plus professional AI-literacy training of youth workers (Education_Professional). Bias axis: only the language barrier from the work's own focus groups (English-only tools, missing Greek support) is coded. Gender and age appear as usage differences reported from a cited survey without a bias analysis and are not coded as axes. Harm: English as default language of AI tools excludes non-English-speaking youth workers and young people (own focus-group result). Mitigation: critical evaluation of AI output to avoid biases is proposed as a competence of youth workers, no evaluation. Gender understanding follows the male/female comparison in Section 3.2 without a definition. Bias understanding is recognisable only as bias inherited from training data. Competence frameworks (DigComp, ETS model, Hofstede's cultural dimensions) frame neither gender nor bias, so no theory reference.

fields.AN_Notes: Other_Axis: marital or relationship status and household composition, analysed through the 'Really Single' model and the broad cohabitation definition. Gender is coded from the own survey with women's shelters on digital exclusion. Religion appears only as a co-mentioned proxy ground and is not coded. Intersectional is not coded, since intersectional discrimination is named in background and recommendations without a result that depends on a combination of axes. Harm types: Direct_Discrimination through citizenship and foreign-affiliation inputs of the 'Model Abroad', Indirect_Discrimination through apparently neutral household, residency and income inputs acting as proxies and through digital-only access, Exclusionary_Norms through dominant-group norms of household and family embedded in the models and the digital-only default. Stereotyping of foreigners as fraud-prone is argued as a political narrative rather than a system output and is left uncoded. No group-level quality difference could be measured because demographic data was denied, so Disparate_Performance is not coded. Mitigation: proposed ban on citizenship and foreign-affiliation inputs (Pre_Processing) and proposed caseworker training, impact assessments, audits, transparency, independent oversight and non-digital access (Organisational_Process). UDK's equalisation of true positive rates is reported and criticised, not presented as an evaluated mitigation. Gender is treated through women in crisis centres without a definition or recognisable understanding; the glossary enumeration of sex, gender identity and intersex status is a legal list that the analysis does not follow. Theory references: structural discrimination and othering frame the treatment of bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Bias axis: race and ethnicity structure the synthesis (racial equity reports, race-ethnic risk thresholds, overrepresentation of Black children). Gender appears once as a subgroup dimension of included studies and socioeconomic status once in a cited co-mention, neither developed, so both are left uncoded. Harm types follow the review's own synthesis: equity in subgroups (Table 3) and subgroup error rates as Disparate_Performance, historical bias in administrative records and overrepresentation driving screening decisions as Indirect_Discrimination. Mitigation: feature selection and exclusion of bias-prone variables (Pre_Processing), group-specific threshold adjustment (Post_Processing), stakeholder engagement, training against automation bias and external ethics reviews (Organisational_Process). Evaluated refers only to the post-processing fairness correction of Purdy and Glass (2023), synthesised by the review with a reported reduction of false positive and false negative error rates among four subgroups; it is not the review's own experiment, and the other strategies remain proposals or descriptions. Bias definition: the review adopts Russell's (2015) equity criterion of consistent prediction across subgroups as part of its analysis frame. Theory reference: ethical frameworks of Russell (2015) and Drake et al. (2020) combined with CFIR frame the assessment of fairness and equity; feminist and critical theories appear only as an outlook.
